title: Simple, efficient and economical methods for isolation and estimation of novel isoflavone using RP-HPLC
author: Alam, Naik, et al.
materials: Solvent-solvent extraction technique was adopted for the isolation of novel compound. In continuing with this technique the rhizomes of Iris kashmiriana Baker were dried, chopped, and powdered (500 g). The extraction of powdered drug was done with petroleum ether (60–80) using a Soxhlet apparatus (24 h run). The petroleum ether extract (gums and resins 2.13 g) was obtained and the marc (400 g) was subjected to extraction with 95% methanol using a Soxhlet apparatus (24 h run). The methanolic extract (5 g) was subjected to successive fractionation with toluene, chloroform and ethyl acetate and n- butanol [1]. On the basis of phytochemical screening results, the glycoside was present in n- butanol fraction. The n-butanol fraction (1.5 g) was taken in dried methanol (80%), passed through activated animal charcoal. The acid hydrolysis was carried out in the presence of 5% HCl (the reaction mixture was refluxed for 2–3 h at 45–50 °C and kept for night) [2]. Completion of reaction was monitored on TLC (10% Methanol in Toluene). The solution was poured into water and the mixture was separated out by separating funnel. From organic layer, the solvent was removed by distillation and residue was further dried. The identification of compound was confirmed by TLC in chloroform: methanol 9:1 with Rf value 0.65 [3]. The structure of the compound was characterized and established by various spectroscopic techniques viz, UV, IR, 1HNMR, 13CNMR, Mass spectrometry and 2D NMR. Furthermore, the compound was also characterized by chemical methods by shift reagents (AlCl3 and CH3COONa) using UV spectrophotometer [4]. Finally, the compound was considered as an aglycone/isoflavone (250 mg). The aqueous portion of the above was subjected to paper chromatography [5] using n-butanol, acetone and water in the ratio 4:1:5, where it was clearly observed that the sugar attached was glucose, with Rf value 0.68.

steps.title: Prepare plant material
steps.instruction: Dry the rhizomes of Iris kashmiriana Baker, chop them, and grind to a fine powder (500 g).

steps.title: Extract with petroleum ether
steps.instruction: Extract the powdered material with petroleum ether (60–80 °C boiling range) in a Soxhlet apparatus for 24 h; collect the petroleum ether extract (gums and resins, 2.13 g) and retain the marc (≈400 g).

steps.title: Extract marc with methanol
steps.instruction: Extract the remaining marc (≈400 g) with 95 % methanol in a Soxhlet apparatus for 24 h; collect the methanolic extract (5 g).

steps.title: Fractionate methanolic extract
steps.instruction: Subject the methanolic extract (5 g) to successive solvent fractionation with toluene, chloroform, ethyl acetate, and n‑butanol; retain the n‑butanol fraction (1.5 g) which contains the glycoside.

steps.title: Adsorb on charcoal
steps.instruction: Dissolve the n‑butanol fraction (1.5 g) in 80 % dried methanol and pass the solution through activated animal charcoal to remove impurities.

steps.title: Acid hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Add 5 % HCl to the charcoal‑treated solution, reflux for 2–3 h at 45–50 °C, then let the reaction stand overnight; monitor completion by TLC using 10 % methanol in toluene as developing solvent.

steps.title: Separate layers and dry
steps.instruction: Pour the cooled reaction mixture into water, transfer to a separating funnel, collect the organic layer, remove solvent by distillation, and dry the residue.

steps.title: Confirm compound by TLC
steps.instruction: Run TLC of the dried residue in chloroform:methanol (9:1); the target compound shows Rf = 0.65.

steps.title: Characterize aglycone
steps.instruction: Characterize the isolated aglycone (250 mg) by UV, IR, ¹H‑NMR, ¹³C‑NMR, 2D‑NMR, mass spectrometry, and by chemical shift‑reagent tests (AlCl₃ and CH₃COONa) using a UV spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Identify sugar by paper chromatography
steps.instruction: Subject the aqueous portion to paper chromatography using n‑butanol:acetone:water (4:1:5); the sugar spot (glucose) appears with Rf = 0.68.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC sample
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg of the isolated compound in 100 mL methanol to obtain a 100 ppm solution; dilute appropriately to obtain a 10 ppm solution for injection.

steps.title: Perform RP‑HPLC analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 10 µL of the 10 ppm solution onto an Agilent 1200 binary pump system equipped with a C18 column; use a mobile phase of water:methanol (45:55), detect at 338 nm with a DAD detector; record retention time (11.2 min) and purity (98.9 %).

steps.title: Recrystallize and determine melting point
steps.instruction: Recrystallize the aglycone from methanol, then measure its uncorrected melting point (225–227 °C).

steps.title: Conduct elemental analysis
steps.instruction: Determine elemental composition; found C 64.00 %, H 4.03 %, O 31.97 % (calculated C 63.21 %, H 3.40 %, O 30.83 %).

steps.title: Record IR spectrum
steps.instruction: Record IR (KBr) spectrum; note peaks at 1518 cm⁻¹ (Ar‑C=C), 1659 cm⁻¹ (C=O), 3080 cm⁻¹ (Ar‑C‑H), 1372 cm⁻¹ (C‑O), 2825 cm⁻¹ (C‑H stretch), 3368 cm⁻¹ (Ar‑OH).

steps.title: Obtain mass spectrum
steps.instruction: Record TOF‑MS (ES+) spectrum; molecular ion m/z = 301.26 and fragment ions at m/z 301, 294, 285, 269, 253, 237, 208, 201, 187, 178, 162, 146, 136, 117, 107, 85 with relative intensities as reported.
